script_old: You signed the gym waiver, but in New York, that doesn't always mean the gym escapes a negligence claim. New York's General Obligations Law has a section aimed at a specific kind of fine print. If you pay to use a pool, a gym, an amusement park, or a similar recreational place, any agreement that exempts the owner or operator from liability for its own negligence, or its employees' negligence, is void as against public policy and wholly unenforceable. So picture a hypothetical. You pay for a gym membership and sign a waiver saying the gym isn't responsible for anything. Then you get hurt because staff ignored a broken machine. Under this law, that waiver can't shield the gym from your negligence claim. But this is where the internet oversells it. First, the law covers certain paid recreational facilities. Not every sports release or instructional program falls under it. Second, getting hurt doesn't prove negligence. You still have to show the gym was careless, and that the carelessness caused the injury. Third, the gym can still argue you accepted the normal risks of the activity.
